meta.consent: Signed by the parent on 7/18/26 (Form IC-1)
meta.assent: Assent sought before each session using a picture choice. On two occasions the student declined and the session was ended; no data were taken on those days.
meta.referral: The team asked why aggression toward staff continues during independent academic work despite a reward chart, and what should replace the chart in the behavior plan.
meta.team: Classroom teacher, two paraprofessionals, SLP, OT, assistant principal, parent
meta.settings: Room 12 during independent math and writing, small-group instruction, specials, the cafeteria, and the bus line, between 7:30 AM and 2:30 PM across 14 school days
meta.notassessed: Home, the bus itself, and any after-school setting. Aggression is reported at home but no data were taken there.
meta.limits: No functional analysis was permitted: the team could not arrange a condition that evokes aggression on purpose, and the parent declined an analogue analysis. The conclusion therefore rests on a described contingency rather than a demonstrated one. Integrity of the existing reward chart was not measured before this assessment, so its failure cannot be attributed to the procedure itself.
meta.falsify: If aggression continues at the assessment level when the same tasks are presented with an adult seated alongside and escape is not delivered, the escape hypothesis is wrong. If it falls when attention is enriched while the escape contingency is left intact, the hypothesis is also wrong.
meta.next: Build the plan on Form TD-1 around functional communication training with a break card and a programmed delay, and measure implementation on Form TI-1 from the first week. Re-run this summary if an analogue analysis later becomes possible.

src.contrib: Three years of discipline records and two prior BIPs. Every documented incident since 2024 occurred during independent seatwork; none during specials or lunch.

src.method: Indirect: structured interview or rating scale
src.who: J. Newsome with teacher, two aides, parent
src.contrib: Four informants completed the interview independently. Three of the four identified demand contexts; the parent identified denied access at home.

src.method: Indirect: structured interview or rating scale
src.contrib: The parent described the same topography at home but tied it to being told no about the tablet rather than to task demands.

Five days at 30-minute intervals. Occurrences concentrated in the two independent academic blocks and at the return from lunch; near zero during specials, lunch, and the Friday preferred-activity afternoon.

Conditional probability of escape given aggression was .81 against a background probability of .10, a difference of +.71. The attention contingency was flat (+.00) despite attention following 46% of incidents, which is what the raw ABC counts alone would have suggested.

Independent demand and delivered escape survived the method of agreement across 10 occurrences; six other candidates were eliminated. Across eight matched pairs, independent demand was implicated in all eight and delivered escape in six. Daily minutes of independent demand correlated with daily aggression at rho = +0.99.

src.method: Daily rate or duration data with visual analysis
src.contrib: Mean 4.2 per day across the assessment, range 0–9, stable with no trend.
MSWO across five sessions. Tablet 92%, fruit chew 71%, praise 46%.

Tablet access confirmed as a reinforcer (single-operant ratio 4.8, 78% of concurrent choices, PR break point 15.7). Praise did not function as a reinforcer, which may help explain why the praise-based reward chart had no effect; the chart’s integrity was not measured.

hyp.h: Attention from adults maintains the behavior
hyp.how: Conditional probability of attention following aggression compared against its background rate (Form ABC-1).
hyp.what: Attention followed 46% of incidents but occurred about as often in the background samples, giving a contingency difference of about zero. A consequence that is equally likely with and without the behavior shows no contingency with it, so these data do not support attention as the maintaining consequence.

hyp.h: Access to preferred items maintains the behavior
hyp.how: Parent interview raised it for the home setting; tested against the school record on Forms ABC-1 and VI-1.
hyp.what: Denied access was present in only one of ten school occurrences and did not survive the method of agreement at school. The parent report is consistent and no home data were taken, so a second, setting-specific function at home remains open.

hyp.h: Poor sleep or missed breakfast raises the likelihood
hyp.how: Coded as candidate setting events across 10 occurrences and 22 nights of home log (Form VI-1).
hyp.what: Each was absent during at least one occurrence, so neither is necessary. Missed breakfast is set aside. Sleep correlated weakly and non-monotonically with daily rate (rho = −0.28) and is retained as a possible setting event, not as a cause.

hyp.how: Screened against the alone-condition proxy in the background samples and the pattern on Form SP-1.
hyp.what: Aggression requires another person by definition of the topography, and occurred at near zero during unstructured and solitary periods.

beh.def: Forceful contact of the student’s hand, foot, or head with any part of an adult’s body — audible on contact, leaving a visible mark, or displacing the adult’s body part. Contacts separated by less than 3 s count as one.
beh.se: the student has had less than 6 hours of sleep or is returning from an unstructured period
beh.ant: an independent academic demand with the adult withdrawing more than 1 m
beh.cons: removal of the task or withdrawal of the demand within 10 seconds
beh.desired: Completes the assigned independent work with no more support than a peer
beh.desCons: Praise and a chart mark at the end of the period — delayed, and praise did not function as a reinforcer on Form RA-1
beh.alt: Hands the break card to the adult and waits through a programmed delay
beh.altCons: A 2-minute break from the task, delivered within 2 seconds of the delay ending
beh.rationale: The break card takes one movement against the effort of an aggression episode, and it produces the break sooner and more reliably than aggression now does. The delay is faded in from 3 s so the card never loses to the faster route.
beh.notes: Property destruction and screaming are monitored but not targeted; they did not hold together as a cluster with aggression on Form TB-1.

beh.def: Contact of the student’s open palm with the side or top of the student’s own head, audible from 1 m or producing visible reddening.
beh.sub: Not applicable — not automatically maintained self-injury
beh.se: the same setting events as for aggression are present
beh.ant: a repeated independent academic demand after a first refusal
beh.cons: a pause in the demand and the adult moving closer
beh.desired: Requests help or indicates the task is too hard
beh.desCons: Adult support, which the student rarely seeks
beh.alt: Hands the break card and waits
beh.rationale: Same replacement as aggression, because the same consequence appears to maintain both. Treating them separately would teach two responses for one function.
beh.notes: Lower rate than aggression but higher urgency because of injury risk; targeted for that reason rather than for its frequency.
